title: A landing reconciled from a trunk report (T16) records no landed symbol changes and leaves the author's in-progress rows in_progress
claim: completeLanding with reconciled:true skips symbol_changes, while advance/resolve landed with symbol_changes [] supersede the author's in-progress rows, so the two landed paths disagree.
scenario: A landing found on trunk via a trunk report (T16) completes; GET /symbol-changes still shows the author's in-progress rows for that task as in_progress. Reported by the H6 step verifier and the CP3 checkpoint verifier.
design_ref: T16 ('landed effects as far as they still apply'), 2.5

title: The hub silently drops lander symbol_changes entries it cannot record
claim: Entries with a bad key or path, an unknown kind, or past 1000 are dropped with nothing logged or reported, so a hub/lander contract mismatch goes unnoticed.
scenario: The lander sends a symbol_changes entry with a key symbols emits but the hub rejects; the landed report succeeds and the change is silently lost.

title: queueView is recomputed for every landing returned and every event
claim: shownLanding and emitUpdated recompute queueView per landing and per event; listLandings is about 40% of the simulation's CPU, which makes the 2,000-seed simulation take about 160 s and the full test suite about 300 s.
scenario: Profile the lander simulation: listLandings dominates. Caching queueView per write() would make the simulation several times faster.

title: Fix-it reports find no hunks in CRLF files
claim: parseConflictMarkers does not recognise the '=======\r' separator, so a conflict in a CRLF file produces no hunks (and no hunk symbols) in the fix-it report, while conflictRegions in regions.ts handles CRLF.
scenario: git merge-file -p --diff3 on CRLF files emits CRLF markers; parseConflictMarkers returns no hunks for them.

title: resolveInDoubt reads trunk's symbols config from the current trunk tip instead of the landed commit's parent
claim: In resolveInDoubt step 2 the symbols section comes from the fetched current trunk, not from T0, so landed symbol changes can be computed under the wrong enabled/exclude settings.
scenario: symbols.enabled or exclude changes on trunk between the push and the in-doubt resolution.

title: Some landed symbol_changes paths in the lander have no test
claim: resolve {landed} after a stale push (pipeline.ts afterStale), the in-doubt 'already on trunk' path, and the rule that a no-op landing sends [] are untested; mutations there are not caught.
scenario: Remove symbol_changes from the afterStale resolve call: all tests still pass.

title: The simulation's mutation guards have no control runs
claim: Each mutation guard runs under its own tuned fault profile, and no control test shows that same profile staying green without the mutation, so a broken profile that always fails would still count as a catch.
scenario: Make a guard's fault profile itself violate an invariant: the guard test still 'catches' it.

title: claim with path#name misreads a not-yet-existing file as a declaration
claim: splitTarget splits at the last '#' when the suffix is a valid symbol key and the whole path doesn't exist, so `claim docs/a#b.md` for a file not created yet claims docs/a with symbol b.md.
scenario: hub claim 'docs/a#b.md' before creating that file.

title: A Write to a file missing from this worktree is told to use Edit
claim: editScope returns whole_file_write before checking whether the file exists, so the deny reason tells the agent to use Edit on a file it cannot Edit.
scenario: Another agent added src/x.ts and holds declarations in it; this agent's Write of src/x.ts (absent here) is denied with 'use Edit for the parts you change'.

title: hooks-symbols.test.ts depends on test order
claim: Later tests rely on claims and worktree state left by earlier it blocks, so running one test alone with -t fails or tests the wrong thing.
scenario: npx vitest run packages/adapter/test/hooks-symbols.test.ts -t 'denies the same function'

title: who_uses throws for declarations named like Object.prototype properties
claim: whoUses reads entry?.ids[name] on a plain object, so names like toString, valueOf, constructor or hasOwnProperty throw, and the tool error is reported as a hub error.
scenario: who_uses on a method named toString.

title: The feed's impact state survives a hub that comes back on a new database
claim: resetHistory() clears the buffer but not listing, impactJobs or impactTold, so new symbol.changed events are evaluated against the old database's changes until the new seq passes the old listing's seq.
scenario: Hub restarts on a fresh database; the agent's impact notices are wrong or missing for a while.

title: who_uses reports everything as free when the hub's claims cannot be read
claim: When the claims request fails or times out, whoUses treats the list as empty and says 'nobody else holds it: update it yourself', listing every place in callers_free. Unknown is not free.
scenario: Hub down or slow beyond the 2 s budget; who_uses tells the agent to edit callers other agents may hold.

title: The reference cache can be poisoned by a concurrent write
claim: Blob ids are taken for all candidates first and each file is read and parsed later, so a file changed in between gets its new content's identifier index stored under the old blob id, including in the committed index blob shared by other worktrees.
scenario: A file changes between blobIds() and refEntry(); later lookups for the old blob return the wrong identifiers.

title: The 'unacked first' impact order is not really tested
claim: In the test the acknowledged change is also the older one, so newest-first ordering alone passes; removing the isAcked comparator from sortImpacts still passes.
scenario: Mutation: drop the isAcked term in sortImpacts; tests stay green.

title: post-edit claims others are told of a signature change after an edit restores the signature
claim: When an edit brings a signature back to its original shape the hub withdraws the row, but post-edit still says 'you changed the signature ... X holds it and is told of your change ... Record the new shape with decide'.
scenario: Change login's signature, then change it back; the second post-edit text is wrong.

title: Pruning held markers after 7 days can hold the agent twice for one landing
claim: markHeld prunes G/agenthub/held/* by mtime after 7 days, but a landing can stay queued that long when no lander runs (R13), so it can hold the agent a second time, breaking 'at most once per landing'.
scenario: holdTurn on, landing L-7 queued 8 days with no lander; the next Stop holds again.

title: A symbol claim_conflict at land tells the agent to wait on the whole file
claim: When land is refused with claim_conflict over a symbol, the text names a hub_wait on the whole file rather than on the held symbol (path#Symbol).
scenario: Another agent holds src/auth.ts#login; land is refused; the advice is hub_wait files ['src/auth.ts'].

title: Two agents' feeds race to fetch trunk into the shared refs/remotes/origin/main
claim: Worktrees of one repository share refs/remotes/origin/main; both feeds fetch into it at once and one logs 'cannot lock ref'.
scenario: Two agents in worktrees of one clone; trunk moves; one feed logs a lock error.
